inputs.original_text: A South Portland parent of three is apologizing to school staff as another budget shortfall threatens more than 70 positions. That apology says a lot about how families are left to absorb the guilt and worry created by chronic underinvestment. These cuts aren’t just numbers: they put workers’ livelihoods and students’ access to support at risk. Schools need sustained public investment, not a system that makes staff and children bear the cost of institutional failure.
inputs.modified_text: A South Portland parent of three is apologizing to school staff while another budget shortfall threatens more than 70 positions. Families shouldn’t be made to carry the shame for a public system starved of resources, and school workers shouldn’t have to wonder whether their jobs will disappear because of chronic underinvestment. These cuts threaten both livelihoods and the support students rely on. The answer is sustained public investment—not asking staff, children, and families to absorb the consequences of institutional failure.
